analysis.title: GS Lee - Midterm Elections (preview + 3 calls), Asia Conviction list changes, China Banks 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: US midterms are Tuesday. Polling shows national sentiment has swung about 10-11pp toward Democrats, and prediction markets imply high odds Democrats win the House with a wider margin (around 236 seats) than either party has had in several years.

GS expects the data center theme in campaigns to fade after the election. The issue ranks low among voter priorities and state governors are likely to shift attention. Congress might limit data center tax incentives, but a national moratorium looks unlikely under any election outcome.
GS expects congressional focus to shift to AI regulation. A compromise codifying basic federal oversight and self-testing is possible, but restrictive regulation looks unlikely.

GS raised crude forecasts: Dec26 Brent to $105/bbl (from $90) and WTI to $94, 2027 average Brent to $88 (from $80) and WTI to $78 (from $73). The reasons are substantial downside supply risks sustaining a large near-term risk premium and a new global supply disruption allowance for the medium term. Mideast output continues to recover as expected.
US 3Q26 midseason earnings: growth is strong but no longer accelerating. GS sees AI investment spending continuing to grow while the growth rate of AI capex is peaking.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue is still accelerating. Cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT was 54% y/y in Q3, showing increasing signs of return on AI investments.

Elevated investor expectations and crowded positioning set a high bar for share prices going into the quarter. Q3 results also raised investor focus on AI disruption risk, particularly among TMT stocks.
Analysts continued to lift forward earnings estimates this season, but the rate of upward revisions has slowed.
China investor survey: more than half expect growth momentum to hold steady and one-third expect a slowdown. More than half expect similar consumption growth and one-third a further slowdown.

China survey: offshore investors lean toward property-price stability while onshore investors are more cautious. Most view a conventional PBOC policy rate cut over the next six months as a close call. Modest CNY gains are the consensus, with offshore investors more optimistic. Investors are broadly optimistic about AI's growth contribution, but enthusiasm is measured.

China Banks 3Q26 first take: the five large banks beat expectations, with average PPOP growth of 16% y/y and net profit growth of 7% y/y. Stabilizing net interest margins and solid bond investment gains gave capacity for accelerated risk disposal, with provision charges up 47% y/y on average.

GS maintains Buy on CCB and BOC. CCB delivered a clean beat with robust earnings quality. GS believes reasonable earnings growth with contained balance-sheet risks will continue to support sector valuations.
APAC Conviction List November update: adding Elite Material, Yokohama Rubber and JSW Steel; removing NYPCB, Shengyi Tech and HK Exchanges.
GS is hosting three midterm calls on Nov 4: 8am ET first take, 10:15am ET views from DC and the trading floor, 11:30am ET election post mortem.

Rating changes listed: Kia (000270.KS) downgraded to Neutral after a 3Q26 operating profit miss on cost pressures likely to persist. China Jewelry: CTF upgraded to Buy, LF downgraded to Sell. Bicara Therapeutics (BCAX) downgraded to Sell with an $8 PT on competitive pressure in HNSCC.

Asia tech results flagged for the week: Murata, Kioxia, Mediatek, Innolight, CXMT, FII, Panasonic, Lasertec, Yageo, Sumitomo Electric, Mitsubishi Electric, HOYA, Montage, Luxshare, Eoptolink, TDK, Tokyo Electron, Ibiden, Toto. GS also lists a Kioxia read-across with a positive mid- to long-term NAND outlook and a Buy on SEC/Hynix.
